analysis.title: GS Contessa - US EQUITIES COLOR STABILIZING 6 Oct 2026
key_insights: S&P 500 closed +58bps at 7,818 with a $2.8Bn market-on-close imbalance to sell. NDX rose 48bps to 31,224, R2K fell 68bps to 2,827, and the Dow rose 49bps to 51,521. Volume was 16.514bn shares versus a YTD daily average of 18.638bn.

NDX and SPX drifted higher as the macro backdrop stabilized, with crude and rates following a bid to Euro bonds overnight and Bessent commentary. Momentum traded lower for a second straight session and the Russell 2000 was a large laggard.
GS's Power Up America basket (GSENEPOW) rose about 450bps and led the leader board after GOOGL headlines renewed focus on AI-driven power demand. CEG rose 12%.
Hard disk drive stocks sold off. The crowded longs STX and WDC fell 8-10% on another wave of competition concerns tied to Toshiba, and the move spread to semicap equipment (AMAT, KLAC, LRCX).
Biotech fell about 350bps. AVBP dropped 46% on a clinical miss, which was only a small drag on the XBI, and another negative update followed more recently.
Floor activity was a 4 on a 1-10 scale, finishing +670bps better to buy. Asset manager and hedge fund flows skewed to buy, driven by macro and tech pockets, but stayed muted.

The desk (quoting Bartlett) attributes the continued NDX breakout to three drivers: clean positioning (GS PB hedge fund net exposure near a 5-year low, GS Sentiment indicator near multi-year lows), covering of macro products and hedges, and steady dollar concentration into Tech/AI at the expense of the rest of the market. Market breadth is at its lowest level since 2000 while AI fundamental datapoints remain very strong.
Tomorrow's calendar: FOMC minutes and a $39bn 10-year auction on the macro side, with APLD and LEVI earnings and Costco September sales on the micro side.

SPX realized the straddle to the topside for the third day in a row, yet fixed-strike vols failed to catch a meaningful bid. SPX skew compressed again while NDX skew steepened further along the curve.
Index flows split between chasing upside and restructuring. Late in the session a GS customer sold 44k SPY 18Dec26 800 calls to buy 55k 18Dec26 810 calls and 33k 20Nov26 800 calls, paying $15mm.
The desk likes VIX call spreads out to November. It expects vol to stay sticky or drift higher regardless of spot, with asset managers the shortest they have historically been in VIX futures.

The desk continues to like upside in URA and select idiosyncratic nuclear names, with investors severely underexposed and government and corporate investment deals driving the tape. Activity was concentrated in energy renewables (up), memory and biotech (lagging), with downside added in biotech and upside in nuclear.
